about.title: Coronado Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Coronado is a small island city, but defective products cause the same kinds of harm here as anywhere else — a faulty appliance in a home near 4th Street, a failing car part along Silver Strand Boulevard, or a piece of recreational gear used at the beach. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product had a defect and that defect caused harm. That covers design flaws, manufacturing errors, and inadequate warnings, and responsibility can extend to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. If you were hurt by a product in Coronado, keeping the item itself — unaltered, unrepaired, and stored safely — can matter a great deal to a future claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect people who've been injured with an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened and explain the options, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Defective Product Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Burden
items.desc: Under California law, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and that defect caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may give an injured person more than one avenue for recovery.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: An attorney can advise you on how to safely keep the item that caused harm, since it's often central evidence in a design, manufacturing, or warning-defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability rules generally focus on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused your injury, not on the manufacturer's state of mind. An independent attorney can look at the specifics of your situation and explain which theory fits best.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without attempting repairs or discarding it. This is especially relevant in a place like Coronado, where products used at home, on Orange Avenue businesses, or along the Silver Strand may need to be examined later. An attorney can guide you on safe storage and documentation.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with an independent attorney in our network. Attorneys typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
